Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• Sudden-onset left-sided headache with visual aura (zig-zag lines), photophobia, nausea/vomiting, dizziness, no focal neurological deficit.  
• Assessment: Clinician’s working diagnosis – migraine with aura.  
• Differential considerations (from DDx and clinician reasoning):  
  – Migraine with aura: Most consistent with unilateral pain, visual aura, GI symptoms, family history.  
  – Subarachnoid hemorrhage: Less likely given pain severity 6/10 and absence of “worst ever” thunderclap, but needs exclusion if symptoms worsen.  
  – Carotid/vertebral artery dissection: Low–moderate likelihood; unilateral pain & visual disturbance but no neck pain/trauma.  
• Plan discussed:  
  – Trial OTC migraine regimen: ibuprofen (dose not specified) + anti-emetic from pharmacy + sugary carbonated drink (e.g., cola).  
  – Schedule same-day in-person review for full neurological examination; cancel if symptoms resolve.  
  – Safety-net advice: attend A&E/ED or contact clinic if headache worsens, new neurological signs develop, or no relief from medications.  
  – No prescriptions issued during tele-visit.
